title: VA Loans
h2: VA Loan Eligibility: Minimum Service Requirements

faqs.a: Yes, even if you currently have a VA loan, you may be eligible for another VA loan with 0% down. Eligibility depends on your remaining entitlement and the county where you plan to purchase.

faqs.q: What types of properties can I buy with a VA loan?
faqs.a: VA loans can be used for existing homes, new construction, approved condominiums, and owner-occupied multi-family properties up to 4 units.

faqs.q: Can I refinance my current mortgage with a VA loan?
faqs.a: Yes, you can refinance both VA and non-VA loans using either an Interest Rate Reduction Refinance Loan (IRRRL) or a VA cash-out refinance.

faqs.q: Can I use my VA loan for high-end properties?
faqs.a: Yes, VA jumbo loans are available for loan amounts up to $2,000,000 for borrowers with sufficient entitlement. Veterans with full entitlement have no VA loan limit -- a down payment is only required if your entitlement has been reduced by a previous VA loan.

faqs.q: Can I take cash out with a VA loan?
faqs.a: Yes, qualified veterans can access up to 100% of their home’s value through a VA cash-out refinance for home improvements, debt consolidation, or other needs.

faqs.q: What credit score do I need for a VA loan?
faqs.a: While the VA doesn’t set a minimum credit score, most lenders require a score of at least 620. VA loans often offer competitive rates regardless of credit score.
